# QuotaDock AI-readable project index

QuotaDock is a Windows PowerShell + WinForms desktop quota dashboard. It manages separate and merged floating cards for Codex, Grok, OpenCode Go, and custom providers.

## Core facts

- `quota_center.ps1`: provider selection, add/remove custom provider, tray UI, update-check launch.
- `quota_fusion_host.ps1`: the single real host window; independent cards and fused cards share one process/window model.
- `launch_quota_small_widget.ps1`: provider launch and optional sync-process start.
- `opencode_go_background_sync.ps1`: optional direct fetch of the official OpenCode Go console after user-configured current-user DPAPI credential storage.
- `opencode_go_browser_bridge.ps1`: localhost bridge for the Chrome extension.
- `opencode-go-quota-bridge/`: read-only page parser for the official OpenCode Go workspace page.
- `packaging/QuotaDock.iss`: per-user Inno Setup installer.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: tag-based Windows installer build and GitHub Release publication.

## Data and security boundary

The UI reads local JSON snapshots. Never commit Cookie, session tokens, API keys, passwords, real account quota snapshots, logs, or personal absolute paths. Runtime state and encrypted credentials live under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\QuotaDock`.

## Extension points

Add a provider by registering a local JSON source in `quota_sources.json` or through QuotaDock's custom-provider UI. A provider adapter should write 0–100 remaining percentages, reset text, and an ISO `updatedAt`. It must fail closed and never turn a parser error into 0%.

## Release/update behavior

`VERSION` is the source of truth. A matching `vX.Y.Z` tag triggers the Windows installer workflow. The client checks GitHub Releases at most once per 24 hours and shows a user-choice dialog; it does not silently install or upload local data.
